title: Ecology federal permits record: Lawson Pond Dam Replacement (Aquatics 143315)

licence.text: Use allowed with credit and a link; commercial and political use prohibited

rows.label: What the project is
rows.value: The project proposes to remove an existing earthen dam and 18-inch culvert spillway to install a replacement dam and replacement outfall spillway within Lawson Pond on San Juan Island. The Washington State Dam Safety Office (DSO) has determined that the current dam, created in the 1940s, no longer meets modern safety requirements and needs to be replaced. The dam and outfall replacement structures would occur within the same footprint as the existing structures. The outfall spillway of Lawson Pond would be replaced with two 24-inch culverts and a narrow emergency spillway located above the replacement culverts. At least 20 linear feet of the outflow stream channel would be armored with quarry spall rock as an erosion control measure as required by DSO. The armored channel would then be hydroseeded with a riparian/wetland herbaceous seed mix for partial herbaceous cover sprouting between the rocks. During construction, the pond would be temporarily dewatered. The underwater topography slopes uniformly to the dam, and extensive bedrock makes the installation of a cofferdam impractical. Dewatering will also eradicate largemouth bass, which are the only fish present in the Pond according to a 2024 fish survey by West Fork Environmental. Pumps, existing water pipes and temporary hoses would be used to gradually dewater Lawson Pond, and water would be discharged onto the uplands of adjacent farm pastures utilizing an existing water right. The secondary dewatering option in case discharge to adjacent farm pastures is not enough is pumping into upland forests east of Lawson Pond
